guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers are a little less bearish on Stanford than the market, but the matchup makes that disagreement difficult to back. Stanford has struggled to create efficient rushing plays and scoring opportunities, while Wake Forest’s strongest defensive work has come against the run. That could force Stanford to rely on a passing offense that has not produced efficiently enough for us to assume it can consistently compensate.

We also respect what Wake Forest showed offensively through its first two games without treating that small sample as proof of a new baseline. Gio Lopez completed 37 of 59 passes for 575 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions while adding 98 rushing yards and two scores. Carlos Hernandez also produced 253 receiving yards over that span. That combination gives Wake Forest multiple ways to create separation if Stanford cannot sustain drives.

The more interesting part is that Wake Forest’s defense was not dominant across the board. It allowed 380 yards per game through two outings, and opponents converted 13 of 27 third downs. That helps explain why our model keeps Stanford somewhat closer than the market does, but Stanford’s offensive matchup is not favorable enough to turn that difference into sufficient value for us.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Stanford’s early-down offense against Wake Forest’s front. Wake Forest recorded five sacks and 15 tackles for loss through its first two games, and Stanford’s rushing efficiency suggests it may struggle to stay ahead of the chains. If Wake Forest repeatedly creates obvious passing situations, the case for Stanford staying within the market’s expectation becomes much harder to support.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest improved to 2-0 with a 38-36 double-overtime road win over Purdue on Sept. 12, 2026.
On fourth-and-15 in the second overtime, Gio Lopez completed a 15-yard pass to Carlos Hernandez to extend the game; Lopez then scored the tying touchdown and the winning two-point conversion.
Lopez finished the Purdue game 16-of-27 for 225 yards and one passing touchdown while leading Wake Forest with 59 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.
Carlos Hernandez caught six passes for 88 yards against Purdue.
Wake Forest committed no turnovers against Purdue.

opponent_notes.fact: Wake Forest's schedule lists Stanford for Oct. 3, 2026 at Allegacy Financial Stadium in Winston-Salem.

quarterback.fact: North Carolina transfer Gio Lopez is Wake Forest's starting quarterback and one of six team captains.
Through two 2026 games, Lopez completed 37 of 59 passes for 575 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions, and rushed 20 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns.
Lopez previously played under current Wake Forest offensive coordinator Rob Ezell at South Alabama.
While playing for North Carolina in 2025, Lopez completed 18 of 25 passes for 203 yards and two touchdowns in a win over Stanford.
The unofficial projected depth chart lists redshirt freshman Steele Pizzella as the backup to Lopez.

The unofficial projected skill-position starters are Ty Clark III at running back and Carlos Hernandez, Antonio Meeks and Kam Shanks at wide receiver, with Will Loerzel, Landon Morris, Kamrean Johnson and Dominick Barry listed as options at tight end.
Ty Clark III recorded his first career 100-yard rushing game with 105 yards against Akron and scored a rushing touchdown against Purdue.
Through two games, Carlos Hernandez had 11 receptions for 253 yards, an average of 126.5 receiving yards per game.
